evals.query: I wrote a strategy memo for the leadership team but my manager says it 'buries the lead'. The recommendations are on page 3 after a long background section. Can you restructure it?
evals.rationale: Structural problem (buried conclusion), needs Pyramid restructuring, not line-level editing

evals.query: Can you clean up this blog post draft? It's too wordy — lots of passive voice and unnecessary adverbs. The ideas are fine, the writing just needs tightening.
evals.rationale: Line-level prose editing: passive voice, adverbs, concision. Structure is fine.

evals.query: This proposal is going to the CFO next week and I need someone to poke holes in it. Are the claims supported? Is the logic sound?
evals.rationale: Stress-testing claims and logic for executive review, not restructuring or line editing

evals.query: My quarterly update email rambles — it's supposed to cover 4 initiatives but there's no clear hierarchy. The reader won't know what matters most.
evals.rationale: Information hierarchy and MECE grouping problem, structural reorganization needed

evals.query: I have this 6-page Amazon-style memo that needs to be reviewed before the leadership offsite. Make sure the narrative holds together.
evals.rationale: Amazon memo format, executive review, narrative stress-testing

evals.query: Just tighten this up for me — make it better, cleaner, more professional. Here's the draft.
evals.rationale: Generic 'make it better' request maps to copy editing as stated in the description

evals.query: This internal report has good data but the argument doesn't flow — the sections feel disconnected and there's no clear 'so what' at the end.
evals.rationale: Argument structure and flow, missing conclusion synthesis — Pyramid/MECE territory

evals.query: The board deck narrative section claims we'll hit $10M ARR but I don't see how the assumptions connect. Can you check the logic chain?
evals.rationale: Logical gap analysis in claims going to board, stress-testing assertions

evals.query: I need to rewrite this technical doc so it follows answer-first structure — our eng team puts methodology before results and stakeholders stop reading.
evals.rationale: Answer-first restructuring, Minto Pyramid application

evals.query: Make this paragraph less clunky. It has too many 'that' clauses and the sentences are all the same length.
evals.rationale: Sentence-level prose mechanics, not structure or logic

evals.query: I want to write an ad campaign for our new product launch.
evals.rationale: Near-miss: advertising copy is scientific-advertising, not non-fiction/editing/stress-testing

evals.query: Help me outline a short story about a detective who discovers something unsettling about their partner.
evals.rationale: Fiction writing, not non-fiction precision or editing

evals.query: I need to prepare a pitch deck for investors — we're raising a Series A.
evals.rationale: Pitch deck creation, not document editing or stress-testing

evals.query: How should I structure the feedback I'm giving to my direct report about their communication skills?
evals.rationale: Feedback coaching, not writing/editing

evals.query: This writing is clear but it feels emotionally flat — it reads like a textbook. How do I make it resonate more?
evals.rationale: Near-miss: emotional resonance is resonance-engine's domain, not precision/editing/stress-testing

evals.query: Review this proposal document — I need to know if the business case math adds up and if the ROI projections are realistic.
evals.rationale: Near-miss: financial validation is business-case or assumption-audit, not writing quality

evals.query: This competitive analysis section of our memo seems biased — it dismisses our main competitor without evidence. Can you stress-test those claims?
evals.rationale: Stress-testing specific claims in a document for logical gaps and unproven assertions

evals.query: I wrote a one-page executive summary but it still feels bloated. Every sentence should earn its place — help me cut it to the bone.
evals.rationale: Concision and cutting, line-level editing task even though the context is executive

evals.query: My team's engineering RFC has solid technical content but the argument for 'why this approach' is scattered across 3 sections with no governing structure.
evals.rationale: Structural reorganization, argument governing structure, MECE grouping

evals.query: This strategy doc is heading to the exec team. Check it end-to-end: is the logic tight? Are assertions backed? Any gaps in the completed staff work?
evals.rationale: Completed Staff Work doctrine, end-to-end logical stress test for executive audience
